segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Hello, Mrs Sutton.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Come in.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: How are you settling in next door?

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Have all your things from Canada arrived yet?

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: I thought I saw a removals van outside your house yesterday afternoon.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: They came yesterday.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: We spent all day yesterday arranging them.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: It’s beginning to feel a bit more like home now.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: That’s good.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Look, come in and sit down.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Are you alright?

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: You look a bit worried.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: Well, I am a bit.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: I’m sorry to bother you so early, Mrs Smith, but I wonder if you could help me.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: Could you tell me how I can get hold of a doctor?

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: Our daughter, Anna, isn’t very well this morning and I may have to call somebody out.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: She keeps being sick and I am beginning to get a bit worried.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: I just don’t know how the health system works here in England.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: All I know is that it’s very different from ours back in Canada.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Well, I don’t know really where to start.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Let me think.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Well, the first thing you have to do is find a family doctor - sometimes we call them general Tipescripts practitioners as well - and register with him or her.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: If you live here, you’ve got to be on a doctor’s list.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: If you’re not, things can be a bit difficult.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Nobody will come out to you if you’re not registered.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Anyway, they work in things called practices.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Sort of small groups of family doctors all working together in the same building.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Now what you’ve got to do this morning is register with one of them.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: There are two practices near here, so we’re quite well off for doctors in this part of Manchester.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: There’s the Dean End Health Centre about ten minutes’ walk away and there’s another practice in South Hay.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: That’s about five minutes away going towards the town centre.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: We’re registered at the Dean End one, but they’re both OK.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: There are about six doctors in our practice and four in the other.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: So ours is quite big in comparison.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: And the building and everything’s a bit more modern.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: South Hay is a bit old-fashioned but the doctors are OK.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Their only problem is that they don’t have a proper appointment system.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Sometimes you have to wait for ages there to see someone.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Anyway, you go to the receptionist in whichever health centre and ask her to register you with a doctor there.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: You have to fill in a form, but it doesn’t take long.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Ours is called Dr Jones and we’ve been going to him for years - ever since we moved here fifteen years ago.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: I wouldn’t say he’s brilliant but I suppose he’s alright really.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: We’re used to him now.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: They say he’s very good with elderly people, but he does tend to get a bit impatient with children.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Listen, the one who’s supposed to be really good with small children is Dr Shaw.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: I’ve heard lots of people say that.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: She’s young and she’s got small children of her own.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: So you could try registering with her.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: And if her list is full, I heard somebody say the other day that there’s a really nice young doctor at South Hay, a Dr Williams.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: He holds special clinics for people with back trouble.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: If you want a doctor to visit you at home, you have to ask for a home visit.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: You’re supposed to do that before 10.30 in the morning, but obviously, if it’s an emergency, you can phone at any time, night or day.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: It might not be your doctor that comes, though.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: It’s quite often one of the other doctors in the practice.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: It doesn’t really seem to make much difference.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Otherwise you make an appointment to see your doctor at the health centre.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: You usually get seen the same day.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Not always of course, but usually, as I say.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: They hold surgeries between 9 and 11.30 every weekday, Q!8 and from 4 to 6.30 Monday to Thursday.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Saturdays are only for emergencies.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: When the doctor sees you, he gives you a prescription.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: He writes what medication you need on it and you take it to a chemist’s shop.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: There’s one opposite the centre.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: If it’s for a child under 16, you don’t have to pay.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: So if it’s for Anna. there’s no problem.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: The same thing goes if you’re unemployed or retired, or if you’re pregnant.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Just as well because it’s not cheap.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: You pay the same price for each item the doctor has prescribed.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: At the moment it’s something like £5 per item.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: So you pay for the medication but the consultation with the doctor doesn’t cost you anything.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: It’s completely free as long as you’re a resident here.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: You’re going to be here for three years, aren’t you?

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: So there shouldn’t be any question of you paying anything to see the doctor.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: So that’s one less problem to worry about.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Look, Mrs Sutton.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: If you want, I’ll sit with your daughter for half an hour if you want to go down to the health centre to register.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: It’s no trouble really, don’t worry.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: Are you sure you wouldn’t mind?

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: That would really help me a lot.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: I’ll ask them if they can send someone round later to see Anna.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: I think I’ll try the Dean End Centre.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Good idea.

segments.speaker: MRS SMITH
segments.en: Don’t worry about Anna.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: MRS SUTTON
segments.en: I’ll be back as soon as I can.
